chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Our companions report that shaving the head, other than for Hajj or Umrah, is mutilation (muthlah). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when he fulfilled his rituals, would turn to a town called Sayah and shave (his head).'

key_terms.مُثْلَةٌ: Mutilation (specifically shaving or cutting in a way that resembles disfigurement)

ai.seo_question: Is shaving the head considered mutilation in Shia jurisprudence if not done for Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the jurisprudential status of shaving the head (*halq*) outside of Hajj and Umrah, addressing the debate on whether it constitutes *muthalah* (mutilation). It highlights Imam al-Rida’s (AS) practice of shaving in Sayah after completing rituals, demonstrating that the act is permissible and not inherently mutilating when performed with a valid intention or context, thereby refining the understanding of ritual purity and bodily adornment in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that our companions are reporting that shaving the head regarding other than Hajj or Umrah is a mutilation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to fulfil his rituals, would go to a town called Sayah and shave (his<sup>asws</sup> head)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Our people narrate that shaving one’s head, except for al-Hajj or al-‘Umrah, is like causing deformity.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, after al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah would go to the town called Sayah and shave his head.’”
